To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed data augmentation scheme for geometric deep learning in BCIs, when compared to a state of theart augmentation method, leads to significant improvement in the classification of brain activity, and that it is a highly promising approach for the future of BCIs.

we propose a novel data augmentation scheme for BCI applications based on graph signal processing, and that this scheme is able to significantly improve the performance of graph convolutional neural networks in two different BCI applications.
we propose a novel data augmentation scheme for personalized BCIs based on the multiplex modelling of multichanel EEG signals and the application of a graph variant of Empirical Mode Decomosition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the exploitation of geometric deep learning for the analysis of multichannel electroencephalography (EEG) signals.
the development of a data augmentation scheme for geometric deep learning that is tailored to the needs of the BCI community.

the following questions: (i) How can we augment brain data in a principled way that is compatible with geometric deep learning? (ii) How can we exploit geometric deep learning for improving brain decoding?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed scheme is an effective and promising method for data augmentation of brain signals and can be successfully combined with geometric deep learning to achieve substantial improvements in BCI applications.
the proposed augmentation scheme can be used to increase the performance of a BCI system by increasing the amount of training data.
the proposed data augmentation method can be used to improve the performance of a GCNN based brain decoding model, as compared to other data augmentation schemes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our proposed scheme for data augmentations is an important asset towards creating robust and reliable brain computer interfaces.
we have shown how the proposed data augmentation scheme can be used to improve the performance of geometric deep learning based BCI systems.

we have proposed a novel method that combines the multiplicity of the brain signals with a non-parametric graph variant of the EMD and we have shown its potential when used in conjunction with Graph Convolution Networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a graph variant of EMD in combination with GCNNs is a promising approach towards the development of personalized BCIs.
the proposed data augmentation method is a promising tool for improving the performance of GCNNs in the context of personalized BCIs.
data augmentation is a powerful tool that can be combined with geometric deep learning in a synergistic fashion.
